summary: Make governed artifact identity stable across checkout conversion and bind review credit to clean committed Git state.
reason: Raw working-tree byte hashing made the same committed Git content acquire different identities after checkout line-ending conversion. Revision 1 found the symlink identity defect. Revision 2 completed the full bounded Adversarial review and drove the clean committed-tree/mode-aware correction. Revision 3 completed another full bounded pass and found staged-new ABSENT ambiguity, unsupported ident/working-tree-encoding transforms, ambient Git routing/replace-ref influence, and core.filemode suppression of POSIX executable mismatch. Those blocking findings were corrected together: HEAD-absent paths now require an empty index entry, unsupported content transforms fail closed, Git subprocess routing environment is sanitized with replacement objects disabled, and POSIX owner-executable state is checked directly regardless of core.filemode. Revision 4 reopens Adversarial against that corrected snapshot. Revision-2 malformed handoff evidence remains only as immutable reservation evidence and receives no semantic credit; revision-3 failure evidence is validly preserved.

reasons: Revision 4 revalidates the bounded artifact-state identity control after all blocking findings from the complete revision-3 Adversarial pass were corrected together.

The complete bounded pass covers committed tree/index/worktree agreement, staged-new absence, path canonicalization, line-ending conversion, unsupported content transforms, Git environment/replace isolation, file mode, symlinks, incomplete checkout, stale credit, and historical evidence preservation.
